issue_context.title: Set highlight parameter max_analyzed_offet to index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset
issue_context.body:
### Description

Use value of `-1` for a highlight request `max_analyzed_offet ` to mean  “look at the [index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/index-modules.html#index-max-analyzed-offset) param and use that


-  Highlighting a text field with length > index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset throws an error.
-  Using  a highlight request parameter max_analyzed_offet with a value =  index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset will ensure that only up to  `index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset` characters get highlighted and no error is thrown (maximum allowed) 
- Using a value of `-1` for  a highlight request  parameter will mean `max_analyzed_offet  =  index.highlight.max_analyzed_offset`
comments:
Just a note, the docs need to be updated with the new behavior.
https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/index-modules.html#index-max-analyzed-offset

review_comments:
I considered making tactical changes and perhaps this would indeed be more expedient, but...

Since there are actually four ways that I count to use the queryMaxAnalyzedOffset, it seemed appropriate to consolidate the behavior. We want passing -1 to mean the same thing (getting the max value of the index offset) independent on the location, and centralizing the logic into a class seemed the right way.

On particular problem I ran into, was that AnnotatedTextHighligtherTests, the test code grabs the constant and sends directly to Lucene, and another copy of the constant goes to another pathway... 

Anyways, if there is strong opposition I can inline
Thanks for the explanation, I agree with your approach, it makes sense to keep the consolidated logic.
